chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Ernie Fields recruits him
summary: Wild Bill Moore appears in Tampa, and Ernie Fields's men hear him and persuade the leader to hire him.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So in the meantime, I am still working over at Wat Sanders' Blue Room. And another old friend of mine, Wild Bill Moore, appeared in town with Christine Chapman, the lady...a fine boogie-woogie pianist. She had a big hit at the time called "Naptown Boogie" -- she was out of Indianapolis. So it was nice to see Wild Bill again.

So I'm still doing my trip, and Ernie Fields' Orchestra came to town. And some of the guys came down to the Blue Room and heard me play. They would come in every night. They must have been around there four or five days, and they'd come in and they'd listen to me play. So they went back and really vouched for me to join the band, you know, with Ernie Fields -- talked to Ernie about me. So they got him to come down and hear me. So he gave me a talking... [LAUGHS HEARTILY] He called everybody Dip. He says "Now,
Dip," he says, "a lot of the guys think you would be an asset to the band" and blah-blah-blah-blah.

So I said, "Well, look, I'm headed to New York"... Because my father had been over and told me he thought I should go in to New York and give myself a good chance, and gave me the money to go to New York and everything. So I told Ernie, "Look, I'm headed to New York actually." So he said, "Well, that's perfect, because we're going to Washington, D.C., and you can work your way up with us, and when you get to Washington you can leave and go over to New York, and you'll have more money." Which made good sense, you know. I said, "Well, good."
So I told my situation to the guys, and they said "Well, good." They were glad to see me go, see. We went...
Yeah, the leader split! They carried on, because a lot of guys have told me about since then that they really kept things going, you know.
